definition.purpose: Separate what can be seen from what is inferred, so you stay curious instead of diagnosing.
definition.instruction: A teacher notices a student, Taylor, during a lab. Sort each statement. You can skip this activity at any time.
definition.accessibility_alternative: Each statement has its own labeled select menu; no dragging is needed.

categories.label: Observation
categories.hint: Something you could see or hear and record without interpreting.

categories.label: Interpretation
categories.hint: A meaning someone attaches to what they saw.

categories.label: Diagnosis
categories.hint: A clinical label that only a qualified professional can assess.

categories.label: Assumption
categories.hint: A claim about causes or history with no information behind it yet.

items.text: Taylor has not opened the notebook for 20 minutes.
items.why: It can be seen and timed. It says nothing about why.

items.text: Taylor doesn't care about this class.
items.why: This attaches a motive to the behavior. Disengagement has many possible causes.
Only a qualified clinician can assess this, and nothing observed here would establish it.

items.text: Something bad must have happened at home.
items.why: It invents a history. Taylor could be tired, ill, upset about a friendship, or something else entirely.

items.text: Taylor said, 'Leave me alone,' when nudged.
items.why: A direct quote is an observation. What it means is a separate question.

items.text: Taylor is shutting down because of past trauma.
items.why: It claims both a mechanism and a history. Neither is supported by what was observed.
'Seems' signals an impression. It is not a diagnosis, but it still goes beyond what was observed.

items.text: Taylor's head has been down since class began.

definition.debrief: A responsible next step is to describe what you saw, hold your interpretations lightly, and ask Taylor what would help.
